static_traits.name: Xu Shan
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, raising two pet dogs
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with friends sharing the same hobby strained by lack of confidence; not yet expressing and discussing true feelings with friends
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problem history; no prior psychotherapy or counseling; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, willing to cooperate, positive attitude; self-reported anxiety; able to self-reflect

basic_info.main_problem: Long-term feelings of incompetence and inadequacy in my beloved photography hobby, starting two years ago after comparing with professional photographers, and gradually worsening; often feeling lack of motivation and Self-doubt when taking photos, with decreased interest.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to identify and challenge negative thoughts, practice cognitive restructuring, regain interest and confidence in photography, and no longer let Self-denial affect life and other areas.
growth_experiences: Started comparing my work with professional photographers' work two years ago, gradually developing and reinforcing feelings of 'not good enough / not competent': initially moderate pressure, which rose steadily with continued comparison and Self-doubt; every photo session brings negative emotions and decreased drive, with markedly reduced interest; relationships with like-minded friends became strained by lack of confidence.

Repeatedly receiving friends' positive feedback on the work, but the client often considers it mere politeness and denies its authenticity, thus gaining little self-worth from positive feedback; this pattern further weakens motivation to share and practice.

core_beliefs: I am not good at photography / I am terrible
I am inferior to professional photographers and can never reach their level

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my photos have not reached professional photographers' level, it shows I am not good enough and very incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Watching tutorials, repeatedly practicing different techniques to prove I can improve
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My work is inferior to theirs; I just cannot do it

special_situations.event: Receiving friends' positive comments on one's photos
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Friends' praise is just politeness; it does not show I shoot well
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Dismissing positive feedback, sharing work less to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite; this does not count

special_situations.event: When reviewing recent photographs, only notices the flaws
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a photo has any flaw, it shows I have not improved and am overall terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses on correcting errors and technical details, ignoring existing progress and strengths
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My photos are full of problems everywhere

special_situations.event: Considering sharing work with a wider audience
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once criticized, it proves I am bad and I will feel worse
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids public sharing, only tries within small circles to lower risk
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Everyone will criticize me; I will get worse

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen and recognized as a capable photographer, receiving genuine positive feedback
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being criticized and dismissed, thereby confirming 'I am not good enough' and feeling ashamed
defense_goal: Reducing the likelihood of being criticized by sharing publicly less and dismissing positive feedback
Maintains a sense of control through technical analysis and self-reproach, avoiding touching vulnerable self-worth issues

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a beginner / one easily dismissed
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges (professional photographers / potential audience / friends)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others (including the counselor or friends) give positive feedback or suggest publicly sharing the work
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing the other person is just being polite, with truly negative views; sharing publicly equals exposing my own inadequacy
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Dismissing positive feedback with euphemisms, emphasizing the work's flaws, offering various reasons to postpone or avoid sharing.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When probed about the photography experience or discussing how to improve photography
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributes the problem entirely to a technical gap, downplaying or circumventing feelings about shame and self-worth
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses an analytical tone, listing technical improvements and learning plans, avoiding expressing vulnerable emotions.

manifestations: The joy of photography eroded by persistent Self-denial
outcomes: Reduced pleasure and sense of meaning

manifestations: Living alone and not yet discussing true feelings with friends
Sharing less for fear of external judgment

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Worries a broader audience will criticize one's work
Interprets friends' praise as politeness rather than genuine appreciation

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Treating professional photographers' standards as the only valid evaluation system
Says to oneself 'I must have done something wrong', constrains oneself with perfectionist demands

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Overly cautious when sharing works, tends to only try within small circles

positive_force: Has some interest in and commitment to photography (although it has declined recently)
Willing to seek help and actively cooperate with counseling (positive attitude)
Already tried improving skills through tutorials and practice
Has like-minded friends and a potential support network
Stable work performance; relatively orderly life structure
negative_force: Excessive comparison and black-and-white thinking, heavily dependent on professional standards
Dismissing positive feedback; seeking external validation leading to fragile self-worth
Catastrophic predictions about criticism and avoiding sharing
Mental filtering when reviewing work, seeing only flaws
Insufficient confidence and persistent self-doubt; decreased interest and drive

target_behavior.behavior: Self-denial and decreased drive when taking photos (accompanied by anxiety and frustration)
antecedent: Comparing my work with professional photographers
target_behavior.core_reason: Forming the core belief 'I am not good enough' under long-term comparison, accompanied by cognitive biases such as black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization
target_behavior.function: Avoids failure and negative evaluation, maintaining fragile self-esteem and a sense of safety
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased interest in photography, reduced practice frequency, limited skill improvement

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids publicly sharing work and seeking broader feedback
antecedent: Considering sharing work with a wider audience
After receiving friends' positive evaluations, worries about being criticized
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic predictions about criticism and over-reliance on external evaluation, dismissing positive evidence to protect the self
target_behavior.function: Avoiding shame and the risk of being dismissed
target_behavior.consequence: Relationship tension with like-minded friends, reduced external support and learning opportunities, persistent negative beliefs
